summary: Eternal runs Zomato for restaurant orders, Blinkit for delivered shopping, District for dining and entertainment, and Hyperpure for supplies used by restaurants.
description: Think of ordering dinner through Zomato, buying groceries through Blinkit, booking an outing through District, or running a restaurant that buys ingredients from Hyperpure. These are different jobs for different customers, even though they belong to the same group.
money: The businesses earn through their own charges, such as fees for arranging orders, advertising, ticketing services or selling goods. They also pay for delivery, stock handling, staff, buildings, technology and promotions. The total checkout payment is not necessarily the amount the group earns.
customers: Households use the consumer apps. Restaurants and other food businesses buy Hyperpure ingredients and supplies. Restaurants, sellers and advertisers can also pay for services that help them reach customers.
drivers: Customers placing repeat orders, how much they buy, what the business earns from each transaction, the cost of delivery and handling, and the money needed for new sites and stock.

groups.title: Zomato: ordering a restaurant meal
groups.explanation: The restaurant cooks the food. Zomato helps the customer find it, place an order, pay and receive delivery. Part of the payment belongs to the restaurant and other service providers; collecting the bill does not mean keeping it all.

groups.title: Blinkit: shopping delivered from nearby
groups.explanation: Workers pick and pack goods at a nearby storage site, often called a dark store, then arrange delivery. Unlike a normal shop, the site mainly serves online orders. The business needs available stock and enough nearby orders to support the running costs.

groups.title: District: arranging a place to go
groups.examples: Dining, entertainment, events and related bookings.
groups.explanation: A customer may use the service to reserve a dining experience or buy access to an event. The venue or organiser provides the experience; booking, payment, advertising and customer service are different jobs from delivering groceries.

groups.title: Hyperpure: supplying a restaurant’s kitchen
groups.examples: Ingredients, kitchen supplies and related delivery services.
groups.explanation: Imagine a restaurant buying ingredients for the meals it will cook. Hyperpure arranges supplies and delivery to that business. Stock, storage and transport costs must be covered even if the goods create a large sales total.

basics.title: An order’s value is different from the company’s own revenue
basics.text: Order value describes what customers buy on the stated basis. Revenue is the amount the company records as its own sales or service income. Where it only arranges a purchase, much of the customer’s payment belongs to the restaurant or seller.

basics.title: Owning goods changes what is recorded
basics.text: Selling goods the business owns is different from charging a fee to arrange another seller’s sale. It can record the goods sale rather than just a service fee, but it must also pay for the goods. A larger recorded sales total is not automatically extra profit.

steps.title: Receive a specific request
steps.text: A customer orders a meal or goods, makes a booking, or a restaurant orders supplies.

steps.title: Arrange the right provider or stock
steps.text: Send the meal request to the restaurant, locate goods for picking, or confirm the booking with the venue.

steps.title: Complete the order and divide the payment
steps.text: Deliver goods or complete the service and pay the amounts owed to restaurants, sellers and other providers under their terms.

steps.title: Cover costs and fund the next order
steps.text: Pay the delivery, site, staff and technology costs. Goods owned by the business need funding before they are sold; new locations also require spending.

specifics.title: Blinkit’s change in goods ownership affects the sales comparison
specifics.text: Eternal’s disclosures explain a move towards Blinkit owning inventory, meaning goods held for sale. Recording the full goods sale rather than only a fee can raise reported revenue without the same increase in items ordered.

specifics.title: Nearby repeat orders help a delivery site
specifics.text: Rent and staff must be paid even when a site is quiet. More nearby orders can spread those costs, but a new location may take time to attract enough customers. More sites do not automatically mean more profit.

specifics.title: A profitable order does not pay every company bill
specifics.text: A measure focused on individual orders can leave out offices, technology, equipment wear, financing or other costs. Read what a headline measure includes before treating it as the profit of the whole group.

watch: Are customers buying more, or has the way sales are recorded changed?
Owned-goods sales and fees for arranging purchases are different measures.

Read the explanation of Blinkit’s stock-ownership change alongside orders and purchase value. Compare matching periods and definitions before concluding that demand grew as quickly as reported revenue.
Do people keep using the services without ever-larger discounts?
Repeat demand and subsidised purchases can have different costs.
Read order frequency, paying-user activity and spending on promotions. Downloads or registrations alone do not show that customers return, and membership benefits still need to be paid for.
Are Blinkit sites attracting enough nearby orders?
Rent, workers and delivery costs continue while a new site finds customers.
Read how older and newer sites perform, what goods are available and the cost of picking and delivery. Check stock losses and storage costs as well as the number of sites opened.
Which businesses earn money after their own costs?
Meals, retail goods, bookings and restaurant supplies have different cost structures.

Read each business’s result using its stated definition, then the further costs needed to reach group profit. Do not assume a large Hyperpure goods-sales total means it earns more than a smaller fee-based service.
How much cash do new sites and stock need?
Growth can use money before it produces enough customer payments.

Read cash from day-to-day operations with spending on sites, equipment and goods waiting to be sold. Check leases, which are rental commitments, and other payment obligations rather than relying only on expansion announcements.
risks: Competition makes orders costly to win
Discounts, advertising and customer benefits can use up the benefit of higher demand.
Orders are unavailable, late or wrong
Poor stock availability, packing, delivery or booking service can discourage repeat use.
Goods tie up money or lose value
Owned stock must be funded and may spoil, become damaged or remain unsold.
Trust and operating rules are breached
Food safety, consumer protection, worker arrangements and data or app failures can cause costs and disruption.
context: The restaurant customer can be on both sides of the group

A restaurant can receive a household’s meal order through Zomato and separately buy ingredients from Hyperpure. These are different transactions: one helps sell a meal, while the other supplies what the kitchen needs to make meals.
quiz: If Blinkit starts owning goods instead of only arranging sales, does a larger revenue figure prove the same increase in demand?
No. Recording the full goods sale changes the revenue basis. Check quantities and order activity as well as the cost of buying and supplying those goods.

financialNotes.title: Keep the segment-result and inventory bases attached
financialNotes.text: The existing verified table uses external-customer revenue and the financial statement’s segment result. Blinkit revenue after the inventory-model change cannot be compared directly with a marketplace commission total as if the two measured the same activity.

financialNotes.title: Largest revenue is not largest earnings
financialNotes.text: The disclosed food-delivery result and the quick-commerce revenue answer different questions. Preserve losses in the other rows, exclude internal transactions as the source does, and reconcile segment results to company profit rather than calling them net earnings.
